summary: GPU-backed detector inference, trained quality parity and resumable dataset processing passed on gpuserver.

profile.installation: Fresh isolated project venv. Torch 2.14.0+cu126 and onnxruntime-gpu 1.24.4 satisfy the declared GPU version ranges. GPU ORT replaces the overlapping CPU onnxruntime distribution, so this is a managed GPU profile, not an unmodified resolver install. Existing environments and the host driver remain unchanged.

earlier_exploratory_profile.conclusion: Genuine CUDA execution, but below the declared GPU minimum. The supported-range profile repeats every probe and supplies the final evidence.

exploratory_profile.quality: Two cleanup attempts retained the 8.125 MiB cuBLAS workspace. Explicitly clearing that workspace made the original allocation assertion pass at zero bytes. Numerical parity had passed in both attempts.
exploratory_profile.corpus: Two fail-closed detector initializations occurred before the harness explicitly enabled allow_network_detectors. A later attempt passed functional assertions but failed JSON serialization of immutable counts. The final fresh run repeats all assertions with dict(counts).
exploratory_profile.runtime: Initial ORT CUDA initialization rejected CPU fallback because shared cuDNN libraries were not on the isolated library path. Adding this venv NVIDIA library directories made the CUDA node assertion pass.

failed_attempts.supported_range_setup: Exact GPU version 1.24.2 is not published on PyPI. Installing 1.24.4 satisfies >=1.24.2. All final functional probes pass on 1.24.4.
failed_attempts.dependency_metadata_check: uv pip check exits 1 only because CPU onnxruntime is absent. GPU onnxruntime-gpu 1.24.4 intentionally supplies the same import namespace. See dependency-check.log and .exit in the frozen bundle. This does not prove an unmodified resolver install.

scope_limits: One tested GPU, driver, Python minor and dependency profile. The prior three-minor CPU qualification remains separate.
GPU-backed execution is proven by real CUDA traces and forwards. Some graph operations and Presidio spaCy processing remain on CPU.
This is functional and numerical validation on synthetic controls, not detection accuracy, GPU throughput, memory capacity, or production qualification.
Python TCP connections are rejected during inference and Hugging Face offline mode is enabled. This is not host-wide network isolation.
GPU corpus verification uses one worker. Parallel GPU workers and GPU routing latency or calibration were not tested.
Large raw traces remain on gpuserver with hashes in the inventory. The repository bundle retains scripts, compact outputs, dependency freeze and attempt logs.

The package metadata still requests the overlapping CPU onnxruntime distribution. GPU validation deliberately installs only the GPU distribution; the metadata check reports this single missing-distribution requirement.
publication_redaction: Unrelated host workload process details are omitted. The private original inventory remains on gpuserver.
